# glinet Provider

Manages GL.iNet routers that run v4 firmware. The provider is tested on a GL-AXT1800 with firmware 4.7.0 and 4.8.3. Other models and firmware versions can have different API methods. Many writes come from the web UI code of firmware 4.8.3 and were not tested on a router: the page of each resource states this.

~> **Warning:** some resources can cut the access to the router, or the Internet access of the router and its clients: [`glinet_access_control`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/access_control), [`glinet_client_allow`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/client_allow), [`glinet_parental_control`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/parental_control), [`glinet_parental_control_group`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/parental_control_group), [`glinet_local_access`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/local_access), [`glinet_wan_access`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/wan_access), [`glinet_wan`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/wan), [`glinet_wan_port`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/wan_port), [`glinet_multiwan`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/multiwan), [`glinet_multiwan_interface`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/multiwan_interface), [`glinet_multiwan_sensitivity`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/multiwan_sensitivity), [`glinet_repeater`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/repeater), [`glinet_lan`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/lan), [`glinet_wifi_interface`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/wifi_interface) and [`glinet_wifi_radio`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/wifi_radio). Read the warnings on their pages before you apply them.

Destroy of a resource disables a feature that exposes the router or acts on its own (`glinet_firewall_dmz`, `glinet_wan_access`, `glinet_ddns`, `glinet_tailscale`, `glinet_zerotier`, `glinet_reboot_schedule`, `glinet_parental_control`), removes a list item (`glinet_lan_static_lease`, `glinet_client_block`, `glinet_client_allow`, `glinet_client_speed_limit`, `glinet_firewall_port_forward`, `glinet_firewall_rule`, `glinet_parental_control_group`, `glinet_parental_control_ruleset`, `glinet_wireguard_client_group`, `glinet_wireguard_client_config`, `glinet_wireguard_server_peer`, `glinet_wireguard_server_route`), and leaves a plain setting unchanged on the router (the other resources).

Each HTTP request to the router has a time limit of 60 seconds. One call can make up to four requests when the session expired: the call, the login challenge, the login and the call again.

Import and sensitive values: after `terraform import`, when the configuration sets a sensitive attribute from a variable with `sensitive = true` (for example `private_key` of `glinet_wireguard_client_config`), the next plan can show an update in-place with no changed attribute. Terraform 1.5.7 does this: the imported state does not mark the value as sensitive, but the configuration does, and Terraform sees this as a difference although the values are equal. It is not known whether newer Terraform versions do this. One `terraform apply` writes the mark into the state, and the next plan shows no changes. In this apply, the provider runs the update of the resource with the values of the configuration. Some resources send no write when the values are equal to the state, for example `glinet_wifi_interface` and `glinet_wireguard_server`. Other resources write all values to the router again, for example `glinet_wan` and `glinet_wireguard_client_config`; what the router does with a write of the same values is not known. `glinet_wireguard_server_peer` also reads `client_config` again with `generate_peer`, and it is not known whether this call makes new keys.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    glinet = {
      source = "ryanrishi/glinet"
    }
  }
}

# The arguments can also come from GLINET_HOST, GLINET_USERNAME and GLINET_PASSWORD.
# With all three set, the block can be empty: provider "glinet" {}
provider "glinet" {
  host     = "http://192.168.8.1"
  username = "root"
  password = var.glinet_password
}

variable "glinet_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `host` (String) URL of the router, with the scheme, for example `http://192.168.8.1`. When it is not set, the provider uses the `GLINET_HOST` environment variable. Defaults to `http://192.168.8.1`. The URL must not contain a user name or a password: use username and password. Each HTTP request to the router has a time limit of 60 seconds. One call can make up to four requests when the session expired: the call, the login challenge, the login and the call again.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password for the login to the router, the same as for the web UI. When it is not set, the provider uses the `GLINET_PASSWORD` environment variable. One of the two is required.
- `username` (String) User name for the login to the router. When it is not set, the provider uses the `GLINET_USERNAME` environment variable. Defaults to `root`.
